# `set_isp_fps`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the global ISP frame-rate setting used by camera operation.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc8580 (64-bit build), SetISPFrameRate @0x14eec0, SetFpsBri @0x14cb20 (ASI_ISP_SetFrameRate / ASI_ISP_SetAutoFrameRate) |

Stores the normalised ISP output frame rate (integer frames per second; 0 selects the camera's automatic frame rate) in a global setting and logs it. No configured value is returned. Out-of-range inputs are normalised to 0 and still succeed. There is no camera, mount or mode guard and no wait. The setter only stores the value; it is applied the next time the preview stream's frame rate is configured (timing INFERRED). One view mode forces 30 regardless, and an internal flag can force automatic.

Side effects: Overwrites the global ISP frame-rate setting. Whether it persists across restart is not established.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_isp_fps"`. [READ] |
| `params` | integer\|array | no | - | Frame rate as a bare integer, or as an array whose first element is an integer (later elements ignored). An object, including one with a key such as fps, is not accepted. Values 0 to 30 are stored as given; negative values and values of 31 or more are stored as 0, which selects the automatic frame rate. The low 32 bits of the integer are used, so values beyond the 32-bit range are truncated rather than rejected. Missing, null, empty array, a non-integer first element, boolean, float, string or object give 104. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | Params missing, null, empty array, or not an integer (bare or first array element) | `expected int param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The range normalisation never produces an error.

## Example

Request, bare:

```json
{"id":101,"method":"set_isp_fps","params":15}
```

Request, positional:

```json
{"id":102,"method":"set_isp_fps","params":[10]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_isp_fps","result":0,"code":0,"id":101}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_isp_fps","error":"expected int param","code":104,"id":103}
```
